column2: Call 112 straight away if there is shortness of breath, wheezing, swelling of the lips or tongue, a hoarse voice, or a widespread rash with floppiness or fainting.
If the child has an adrenaline auto-injector prescribed by a doctor, use it straight away on the outer thigh.
If they’re struggling to breathe, sit them up; if they’re floppy, lay them on their back and raise their legs.
If there’s no improvement after 5 minutes, a second injector (if available) can be given.
Even if they improve, they must be assessed in an emergency department.
Diarrhoea, vomiting and fluid loss

See a doctor or go to A&E for repeated vomiting or diarrhoea in a baby under 6 months; no wet nappy for 6–8 hours; a sunken soft spot, crying without tears, unusual drowsiness; bloody diarrhoea or green vomit.
Keep breastfeeding or formula feeding; offer smaller amounts more often.
Give the oral rehydration solution (ORS) your doctor recommends in small sips.
Keep track of wet nappies and temperature.
Don’t give fruit juice, fizzy or sugary drinks.

In an emergency, first make sure you’re safe, then call for help. Emergency number in Turkey: 112, poison advice: 114. These cards are reminders; we recommend taking a baby and child first aid course.
